sections.overview: Illawarra wisharti is an Australian funnel-web spider and the sole described species of its genus, Illawarra.
sections.identification: Its brown body bears distinct abdominal chevrons; males have a broad mid-ventral spine row beneath the tarsi of all four leg pairs, while females have a robust first leg with enlarged claws.
sections.habitat: The species is known from the Illawarra region of southern New South Wales.
sections.diet: The taxonomic and collection accounts reviewed here provide no species-specific prey list.
sections.behavior: Its species description is based on preserved specimens and does not establish a detailed activity pattern.
sections.reproduction: The revision describes female reproductive structures, but the sources consulted do not report clutch size or breeding season.
sections.ecology: It is a distinct atracid genus alongside Atrax and Hadronyche; the Australian revision diagnoses it by sex-specific leg characters rather than treating it as an Atrax species.
sections.conservation: The sources document a restricted regional distribution but do not provide a current species-level conservation category.
